kind.description: What the component IS, as opposed to `category`, which is the styleguide sidebar bucket. block = editor-insertable (has block.json); section = page-level chrome, not editor-insertable; element = self-contained and reusable across unrelated parents; part = fragment authored for one specific parent's structure; utility = rendering helper with no visual identity of its own. Drives visual-baseline inclusion, catalogue presentation and Gutenberg eligibility. See tailwind-base ADR 0012.

render.description: Iframe-wrapper mode for the styleguide preview — how the component is FRAMED, not what it is (that is `kind`). Mirrors ComponentParser::RENDER_MODES in parisek/styleguide, which silently defaults an unknown value; this enum makes the mistake loud instead.

description.description: What this component is, written for the EDITOR. Plain language, no implementation detail. Length follows the audience: this field is the editor's full context and may run to several sentences, while `wp.block.description` — the text the Gutenberg inserter panel shows — has to stay a single short one. They are NOT the same string and one does not project into the other. An earlier version of this schema said it did; nothing ever implemented that, and implementing it would push this field's length into a UI budgeted for one line, so the block-facing text is authored explicitly instead. Deliberately not the agent's copy: an AI agent reads `mcp:`, a developer reads `dev:`. The same triad exists at component, layout and field level, so the audience of a line is readable from its key instead of guessed from its wording.

mcp.description: Guidance for an AI agent choosing and filling this component, surfaced through get-block-catalog. Write decision rules and constraints, not descriptions: not "hero is the opening block" but "at most once per page, always first; use section-intro for mid-page sections". Cover when to reach for this component, when NOT to (naming the sibling that fits instead), and its visual weight — full-bleed and loud versus small and supplementary — the one thing that cannot be read out of the field list. Never restate what the consuming plugin's per-type defaults already say; those are composed after these lines, so a redundant entry only dilutes better guidance.

dev.description: Notes for the DEVELOPER working on this component — implementation constraints, gotchas, why something is the way it is. Stays in the YAML: it reaches neither the editor's UI nor the agent's catalog.

wpOverlay.description: `wp:` is a fully open escape-hatch object merged with HIGHEST precedence over every derived/reconstructed prop. Two classes of prop are reserved: scalar identity (`key`/`name`/`type` — a field's WHOLE identity: ACF postmeta key, postmeta name, field-shape discriminator) and structural containers (`fields`/`sub_fields`/`layouts` — which carry the identity of NESTED nodes one level down, so letting `wp:` overwrite them is the exact same hazard one level removed) plus `parent_repeater` (ACF-computed structural metadata re-derived from nesting on every generation; it has no legitimate authoring path at all). Letting `wp:` override any of these gives identity two independent, silently-diverging paths (seven review rounds each found a new bug of this exact shape — round 7 found the ROOT-level `wp:` bag wasn't covered at all, plus the field/layout-level bypasses via the structural props). Use the sanctioned top-level prop instead: `key:` (pattern ^field_/^layout_/^group_) to pin a key, the YAML field-map key (or a layout's own `name:`) to control the name, the top-level `type:` enum to pick the field shape, and the field/layout's own `fields:`/`layouts:` map to author nested content — never `wp:`. `wp.conditional_logic` is deliberately NOT reserved here — see FieldsGenerator's own dangling-reference validation, which is the correctness gate for that prop instead.

multivalueAnnotation.description: Either guidance, or an explicit decision that none is needed. A bare key (`mcp:`, parsing as null) means DELIBERATELY NONE — tooling that reports un-annotated components must stay silent about it, which an absent key cannot express. An empty string and an empty array stay invalid on purpose: they are almost always a half-finished edit, and allowing them would give one decision three spellings.

role.description: Axis B (provenance) from issue #13, completed in #27 — where this input's runtime value comes from. field = authored in the CMS by an editor. query = assembled by the component's own PHP sidecar from the database. global = site-wide options. parent = passed in by the calling template (include/embed). inherited = injected framework-wide into every component; carried by schemas/framework-props-baseline.yaml and never written into a definition. derived = built out of a declared sibling field, and requires `from:` naming that sibling. Who builds it does not matter: the framework's field-formatting layer (`article-video-grid.sources` from `video`) and the component's own PHP lifting a nested value to the root (`reference-slider.title` from `heading`) are the same fact about where the value comes from, and `from:` makes both checkable. Defaults to `field` when omitted, and a descendant inherits its ancestor's role. `computed` was removed in #27: no instance was found across ~200 components that was not `query`.

from.description: The sibling field this one is derived from. Required by `role: derived`, forbidden otherwise. `article-video-grid.sources` is derived from `video` — the field-formatting layer builds the source cascade out of it. Naming the origin is what makes `derived` verifiable rather than a place to hide an unclassified prop: the linter checks the named sibling actually exists at the same level.

of.description: What this field points at, as `<kind>:<name>`. The grammar is closed on purpose — a typo like `components:header-menu` or `post :article` would otherwise validate and then be silently ignored by every linter. Four kinds: `geo`, `term:<taxonomy>`, `post:<type>[,post:<type>…]` (the reference targets AbstractTypeReverseMapper already enforces at generation), and `component:<slug>[#<field>]`. The last means this prop IS that component's input, so its shape lives there: `header.menu` is `of: component:header-menu#items` rather than a transcript of the child's item fields — a transcript is a second place to keep right, and the one in tailwind-base had already drifted. A field carrying a component target declares no `fields:` of its own and must not project into acf.json; nobody edits a value the parent passes through.

open.description: This field is an open map whose keys are not knowable in advance — `picture.link_attributes`, an arbitrary attribute bag merged onto the `<a>`. A `group`/`repeater` normally has to enumerate `fields:`, which forces an author to either invent representative leaves or drop a real input from the contract; tailwind-base did the former and documented the leaves as approximations (docs/398-unresolved-roles.md). `open: true` states the openness instead, and the contract check stops descending at it — what is inside belongs to whoever fills the map. It does not excuse the field itself from carrying a role.

acf.description: Axis A (projection) from issue #13 — whether this field has an ACF-backed representation in acf.json. Derives from `role` when omitted: `field` -> true, every other role -> false, because only an editor-authored value needs an ACF field behind it. An explicit `acf:` always wins over the derivation, which is how a `query` repeater that still needs projecting children declares itself.

allOf.$comment: `type` and `label` describe an ACF field: the widget the editor gets and the caption above it. A prop that projects into acf.json therefore needs both, and one that does not — `role: parent`, `query`, `global`, `inherited`, `derived` — needs neither. Demanding them anyway would mean writing an editor label for a value no editor ever sees, which is noise an author has to delete before the definition reads true. Absent `role:` means `field`, so every definition written before #27 is unaffected.

A group/repeater must enumerate `fields:` — a container with nothing in it describes nothing. Two exceptions: an open map has no keys to declare, and a field borrowing another component's shape declares it there.

A borrowed shape has one home. Declaring `fields:` next to `of: component:` would recreate the transcript this target exists to remove, and leave the check with two answers. The forward must also be non-projecting: `role:` is required and cannot be `field` (omitting it defaults to `field`, which defaults `acf:` to true), so a forward can never reach acf.json with no sub-fields to emit.

description.description: What this layout variant is, for the EDITOR. Same audience split as at component level.

mcp.description: Guidance for an AI agent choosing between sibling layouts of the same flexible-content field. The same decision as choosing between components, one level down: say when to pick THIS variant rather than its siblings, and name the sibling that fits the case you are excluding.

dev.description: Notes for the DEVELOPER about this layout variant. Stays in the YAML.

rootFieldMap.description: Root field map. May be empty (`fields: {}`) for a component with no inputs at all -- but the key itself stays required, so a typo like `feilds:` still fails.
